stage.quote: Voltage Park, which is technically a subsidiary of the Navigation Fund.
stage.note: Not VC-funded in the traditional sense: capitalized by a one-time ~$500M GPU asset contribution from its nonprofit parent, the Navigation Fund (funded by Jed McCaleb), rather than priced equity rounds.

total_funding_usd.basis: TechCrunch: Navigation Fund purchased 24,000 Nvidia H100 GPUs (~$500M, 'worth an estimated half a billion dollars') and contributed them as initial capital to Voltage Park. Voltage Park's own About page separately claims a '$1 billion Long-term capital foundation', which is unconfirmed by press and may include later debt/hardware financing not itemized publicly.
total_funding_usd.quote: Already, the cluster of GPUs — worth an estimated half a billion dollars and among the largest in the world — is being used by startups Imbue and Character.ai

last_round.type: capital contribution (nonprofit-to-subsidiary GPU asset transfer, not a priced equity round)
last_round.quote: McCaleb started a nonprofit called the Navigation Fund to whose endowment he donated. The Navigation Fund then purchased the aforementioned H100s ... and transferred ownership of the GPUs to for-profit Voltage Park

note: Voltage Park is a for-profit subsidiary of the nonprofit Navigation Fund (funded by crypto/aerospace entrepreneur Jed McCaleb), launched Oct 2023 to operate a ~24,000-GPU (Nvidia H100) cloud; McCaleb does not own, run, or profit from either entity per a Navigation Fund spokesperson. Former CEO Ozan Kaya has since moved to become President of Lightning AI, per Voltage Park's team page, suggesting a leadership/organizational change worth confirming with a buyer. No subsequent priced equity round or updated total-funding figure beyond the initial ~$500M GPU contribution was found; the company's own About page claims a '$1 billion long-term capital foundation' which is unverified by independent press.
